record.original_question: For the unified reconstruction method that balances a measurement-fitting term with a penalty tying the reconstruction to a generative model, can one derive sharper theoretical error guarantees under realistic assumptions on the measurement map A, the generative model G, and the ground-truth signal f_0, including cases where A does not satisfy a global bi-Lipschitz property and cases involving specific learned or model-based generative models?

evidence.quote: Problem 5.6. Improve the theoretical guarantees on the reconstruction error for a unified approach (13) under appropriate assumptions on the measurement map A, generative model G, and the ground truth f0. What if A does not have a (global) bi-Lipschitz property? How the bounds in Lemmas 5.3 and 5.5 can be improved for specific classes of learned and model-based generative models G?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be Hilbert (or Banach) spaces. Consider an inverse problem in which one wishes to recover a ground-truth signal $f_0 \in X$ from noisy measurements
$$ y = A f_0 + \eta \in Y, \qquad \|\eta\|_Y \le \delta, $$
where $A : X \to Y$ is a (possibly nonlinear) measurement map. Let $G : Z \to X$ be a generative model defined on a latent space $Z$ (for instance a trained neural network, normalizing flow, or model-based prior), whose range $\mathcal{R}(G) \subset X$ serves as a learned signal class.

For parameters $\alpha,\beta > 0$, consider the unified variational reconstruction
$$ \hat f \in \arg\min_{f \in X} \Big\{ \tfrac12 \|A f - y\|_Y^2 + \alpha \, d\big(f,\mathcal{R}(G)\big)^2 + \beta\, \mathcal{R}(f) \Big\}, \qquad (\star) $$
which balances a measurement-fitting term against a penalty tying the reconstruction to the generative model (here $d(\cdot, \mathcal{R}(G))$ denotes distance to the range of $G$ and $\mathcal{R}$ is an optional regularizer).

Assume baseline reconstruction error guarantees of the form
$$ \|\hat f - f_0\|_X \;\le\; C_1\,\delta + C_2\, d(f_0, \mathcal{R}(G)) + C_3\,\varepsilon(G), $$
which can be derived under a global bi-Lipschitz assumption on $A$ (i.e. there exist $0 < c \le C < \infty$ with $c\|f-g\|_X \le \|Af - Ag\|_Y \le C\|f-g\|_X$ for all $f,g$ in a relevant set) together with Lipschitz/regularity assumptions on $G$.

Problem. Derive sharper theoretical error guarantees for the estimator $\hat f$ defined by $(\star)$ under realistic assumptions on $A$, $G$, and $f_0$. In particular:

(a) Establish quantitative reconstruction error bounds in the case where $A$ does not satisfy a global bi-Lipschitz property — for example, when $A$ is only locally bi-Lipschitz, satisfies a restricted isometry / range-restricted isometry condition on a neighborhood of $\mathcal{R}(G)$, or admits only a one-sided stability (modulus of injectivity / weak-type) estimate.

(b) Improve the constants and rates in such bounds for specific structured classes of generative models $G$, including (i) learned generative models such as ReLU neural network decoders, normalizing flows, score-based / diffusion generative models, and (ii) model-based generative models such as sparse synthesis dictionaries, low-rank models, or analytically prescribed manifolds, exploiting their geometric and approximation-theoretic properties.

State explicit hypotheses on $A$, $G$, and $f_0$ (including how well $f_0$ is approximated by $\mathcal{R}(G)$) under which the improved bounds hold, and identify regimes where the dependence on $\delta$, on the approximation error $d(f_0,\mathcal{R}(G))$, and on parameters of $G$ (depth, width, Lipschitz constant, latent dimension) is optimal.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of obtaining sharp reconstruction-error guarantees for variational inverse-problem estimators that combine a data-fidelity term with a generative-model prior is an active research area. Existing results (e.g., Bora et al.-type bounds, range-restricted isometry conditions, Lipschitz-decoder analyses) provide guarantees under bi-Lipschitz / RIP-like assumptions on $A$ and Lipschitz assumptions on $G$, but sharper bounds for non-bi-Lipschitz $A$ and for specific learned (ReLU networks, flows, diffusion) or model-based generative families remain open and are the subject of ongoing work; no comprehensive resolution has been reported.

status_evidence.title: Theoretical Perspectives on Deep Learning Methods in Inverse Problems
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of reconstruction guarantees with generative priors under Lipschitz / RIP-type conditions on A and G.
status_evidence.claim: Existing guarantees rely on bi-Lipschitz/RIP-style assumptions; refining them for general A and structured G is highlighted as ongoing.

status_evidence.title: Conditional Generative Models are Provably Robust
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes pointwise guarantees for Bayesian inverse problems via conditional generative models with Lipschitz/Wasserstein assumptions.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work continues to develop—but has not closed—sharp guarantees for generative-prior reconstruction under realistic assumptions.
